definitions.explanation: An intensifier used to emphasize the truth or degree of something; often expresses genuine feeling or evaluation.

examples.japanese: {実|じつ}に{素晴|すば}らしい{景色|けしき}だ。
{実|じつ}に{残念|ざんねん}なことだ。
これは{実|じつ}に{興味深|きょうみぶか}い{研究|けんきゅう}だ。

notes:
{実|じつ}に is a formal adverb that intensifies what follows, conveying that the speaker genuinely feels or evaluates something to be true. It often carries a sense of impressed or heartfelt emphasis.

POSITION:
Placed directly before the adjective, adverb, or phrase it modifies: {実|じつ}に{素晴|すば}らしい (truly wonderful), {実|じつ}に{残念|ざんねん}だ (truly regrettable).

REGISTER:
Formal and literary. Common in speeches, essays, and written prose. In casual conversation, {本当|ほんとう}に or すごく are preferred.

CONTRAST:
- {実|じつ}に: indeed, truly (formal, emphatic)
- {本当|ほんとう}に: really (general use, all registers)
- {誠|まこと}に: truly (very formal, humble, used in business)
- すごく: very (casual, colloquial)
